description: We are a multidisciplinary team of students from Manaus, Brazil, with backgrounds in Software Engineering, Computer Science, and Chemical Engineering. United by our interest in technology, innovation, and environmental sustainability, we combine our knowledge, creativity, and diverse perspectives to develop Amazon Fire Calendar. Our goal is to use technology and teamwork to address wildfire challenges in the Amazon and contribute to a better understanding and protection of our planet.
summary:
Amazon Fire Calendar is a bilingual interactive web application designed to monitor and analyze wildfire activity across the Brazilian Legal Amazon. It integrates NASA FIRMS active fire detections from MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m), addressing differences in spatial resolution and satellite observation footprints.

The platform transforms satellite observations into a unified burning activity calendar, featuring interactive maps, historical timelines, seasonal heatmaps, Fire Radiative Power (FRP), and anomaly detection using Z-Scores. Users can explore the Legal Amazon, select specific Brazilian states, or define custom Areas of Interest (AOIs).

By making satellite data easier to interpret and compare, the project aims to support environmental monitoring, scientific research, and early identification of unusual fire activity, helping communities and decision-makers better understand wildfire patterns in the Amazon.
details:
The Problem

Every year, the Amazon faces severe wildfire seasons that threaten biodiversity, public health, local communities, and climate balance. Although satellite fire detection data is available, information from different sensors is not directly comparable due to differences in spatial resolution and observation characteristics.

MODIS provides active fire detections at approximately 1 km resolution, while VIIRS provides detections at 375 m. This difference can lead to misleading comparisons and make it difficult to understand actual changes in fire activity.

Our Solution

Amazon Fire Calendar is a bilingual web platform that integrates NASA FIRMS active fire data from MODIS and VIIRS into a unified burning activity monitoring system.

Its harmonization engine accounts for orbital pixel footprint distortion using Scan × Track measurements, identifies coincident detections between sensors, and distinguishes smaller VIIRS-only detections through configurable weighting.

The application is organized into three main sections:

1. Map & Timeline: Interactive maps, satellite detection points, historical timelines, geographic filters, and custom Areas of Interest (AOIs).

2. Calendar & Matrix: Monthly and weekly burning activity calendars, seasonal heatmaps, Fire Radiative Power (FRP), and Z-Score anomaly indicators.

3. MODIS × VIIRS Laboratory: Interactive sensor comparisons, orbital footprint simulation, and visualization of the harmonization methodology.

Benefits and Expected Impact

The platform makes satellite observations easier to explore and interpret. It helps researchers, environmental organizations, and land managers identify unusual fire activity, examine historical patterns, and better understand seasonal wildfire behavior.

It also provides CSV and GeoJSON exports to support further analysis and operational planning.

Technology and Development

The backend was developed using Python 3.11+, FastAPI, HTTPX, and Uvicorn. The frontend uses React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet, React-Leaflet, Recharts, and Lucide Icons.

The application is deployed using Render and integrates NASA FIRMS data.

Creativity and Innovation

The project's main innovation is its effort to harmonize observations from two different satellite sensor systems rather than simply displaying their detections together.

By combining spatial correction, temporal analysis, interactive visualization, and a unified burning activity calendar, Amazon Fire Calendar transforms complex satellite observations into accessible environmental information.
